title: Fixed rules Search filters the list and keeps the current sort
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919), with the Settings - Parts permission.
  • Category {Category-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC49 widgets) exists.
  • Category {Category-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC49 gadgets) exists.
  • Fixed rule part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC49-AAA-1) is at {Location-A} in category {Category-A} with fixed price (for example 777.77).
  • Fixed rule part {Part-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC49-BBB-2) is at {Location-A} in category {Category-A} with fixed price (for example 12.34).
  • Fixed rule part {Part-C} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC49-CCC-3) is at {Location-A} in category {Category-B} with fixed price (for example 56.78).
  • Search term {Term-A} (for example zzautotest-pc49) is the tag in small letters and matches only these three rules.
  • Search term {Term-B} (for example PC49 WIDGETS) is part of {Category-A}'s name in capitals.
  • Search term {Term-C} (for example 777.77) is part of {Part-A}'s fixed price as shown.
  • You are on a page other than Pricing and the Pricing Search box is empty.
custom_steps:
1. Go to Settings and click Pricing in the Parts group of the Settings menu.
  2. Click the Fixed rules tab.
  3. Wait until the loading indicator on the Fixed rules tab disappears.
  4. Click the Fixed Price column header once, so the highest price is first.
  5. Type {Term-A} in the Search box.
  6. Read every row shown.
  7. Clear the Search box.
  8. Type {Term-B} in the Search box.
  9. Read every row shown.
  10. Clear the Search box.
  11. Type {Term-C} in the Search box.
  12. Read every row shown.
  13. Clear the Search box.
  14. Move the mouse pointer away from the column headers.
  15. Read the Fixed Price arrow and find {Part-A}, {Part-B} and {Part-C}.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 6: only {Part-A}, {Part-C} and {Part-B} are shown, in that order (777.77, 56.78, 12.34, highest first). The small letters made no difference.
  • Step 9: only {Part-A} and {Part-B} (both in {Category-A}) are shown, {Part-A} first.
  • Step 12: only {Part-A} is shown.
  • Step 15: every rule is shown again, the Fixed Price arrow still points down, and {Part-A}, {Part-C}, {Part-B} keep that order.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-11258; story SV-10136 (Story 3, Fixed Rules, sortable columns; story text re-synced to the PRD on 13 Oct 2026); PRD "Settings Pricing And Categories Sorting (Price/Category)", Confluence 578781186, version 21 (14 Oct 2026), S3-R18 (with S3-R8 for the starting sort), read 14 Oct 2026; design canvas board 1.4 (Fixed rules - before and after), 13 Oct copy, unchanged on 14 Oct. Product comment: Chris Ward, 23 Sep 2026 (Confluence comment 882311473), first comment item 3, answer (a): search works on Fixed Rules. Source-verified 14 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Price/Category QA build exists). The technical plan of 13 Oct 2026 (FR-018, FR-020) says the first click on Fixed price sorts lowest first; PRD version 21 (14 Oct 2026, S3-R4, S3-R8) says highest first and is newer, so this case follows the PRD.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R18: “Typing in the Fixed Rules search box filters the loaded rules to those that match the term, and shows them in the current sort. A rule matches when the term appears, ignoring case, in its Part number, Category or Fixed price as shown on screen. Clearing the box shows every rule again, still in the current sort. Today the box does nothing on this tab, because the server ignores the term; the release note says that it now works.”
  • S3-R8: “Fixed price sorts by value. Its first click puts the highest price first.”
